title: Cost & latency slicing + reconciliation service for per-route/model/customer attribution
creator: Marco Reyes
description: Design and implement a stable service that computes deterministic per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns from streaming telemetry and periodic billing metadata. The service must reconcile streaming attributions with batch billing runs, handle late-arriving telemetry, avoid double-counting across fallbacks and multiplexer execution, and provide materialized views and an RPC endpoint for Console queries and Chargeback exports.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline computes per-request token and latency attribution and aggregates to per-route/model/customer daily and hourly views
Reconciliation job identifies and corrects discrepancies between realtime attributions and monthly billing within 1% for top-100 customers
Supports multi-model fallbacks: when a request is served across compatible model variants, cost/latency is attributed proportionally to actual inference execution time and tokens consumed
Handles prefix/KV cache hits: zero-cost attribution to model compute for cached tokens, but still surface cache latency impact in UX
Materialized tables accessible by Console with <=5s staleness for recent 1h and <=1h for 24h windows
Comprehensive unit and integration tests plus a data-quality monitoring dashboard with anomaly alerts
tasks: Spec: define attribution algebra for token vs GPU-time vs batching overhead
Proto: build prototype that consumes telemetry.tokens and routing.decisions topics and emits per-request attribution events
Batch reconciliation: implement nightly job to join billing ledgers and flag mismatches
Materialization: design ClickHouse/BigQuery schema and retention plan
API: add RPC endpoint for Console queries and bulk export for finance
Monitoring: add DQ checks, alert rules, and SLOs for feed latency and reconciliation drift
Rollout: canary on small subset of customers, compare existing ledger for parity
architecture_notes: Input sources: kafka.telemetry.tokens (token counts + model_id + route_id + request_id + timestamp), kafka.inference.exec (GPU ms, batch_id, model_variant, request_ids[]), routing.decisions (selected_model, fallback_chain), statement-of-records from billing-ledge daily CSV
Core compute: two-stage pipeline - streaming attribution (Flink/Beam) for nearline per-request tags, then a reconciliation layer (Airflow job) that applies corrections and emits audited ledger rows

Attribution rules: base_cost = tokens_charged * model_unit_cost; additional_gpu_cost apportioned by inference.exec GPU_ms weighted by request token share in batch; batching overhead amortized across requests in batch by token-weighted share
Fallback handling: attribute actual GPU_ms and tokens to the variant that executed; route-level cost includes routing decision overhead (proxy/serialization) measured via edge latency markers

Caching: KV/prefix hits marked in telemetry.tokens with cache:true and cause token_cost=0 but latency fields still recorded; reconciling with billing to ensure cache savings reflect in finance exports
State & watermarking: use event-time processing with 24h allowed lateness and periodic backfill window; late events routed to correction table and trigger delta re-aggregation
Storage: hot views in ClickHouse for console UX (hour/day rollups), cold audited ledger in BigQuery for finance and legal
Idempotency: all attribution events keyed by request_id and sequence to allow safe reprocessing
Security: PII-free outputs; customer IDs pinned to hashed tenant identifiers for downstream analytics. KMS used for any encryption-at-rest in BigQuery sinks
rollout_plan: Alpha: enable on internal dev accounts and sample-100 customers (1% traffic) for two weeks; compare totals vs legacy aggregator
Canary: 10% traffic selected by shard; run streaming attribution in parallel with legacy pipeline and reconcile deltas daily
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 4 weeks with automatic rollback on reconciliation drift >3% or DQ alerts
Cutover: switch Console API to new materialized view after parity checks and a one-week stability window
Post-cutover: nightly reconciliation window remains enabled for 90 days to capture late-arriving corrections
monitoring_and_alerting: Latency SLO for streaming pipeline end-to-end: 95th percentile attribution emission <= 5s
Reconciliation drift alert: if cumulative cost delta between streaming and monthly billing > 1% for top-50 customers
Data-quality alerts: missing model_id or request_id in >0.05% of events triggers high-priority investigation
Backfill health: track processed backfill bytes and time-to-complete; alert if backfill takes >48h for 7-day window
Runtime errors and tombstones metric with paging if >10/day
